name: Classify viral and microbial sequences by taxon
description: Which method assigns a viral or microbial DNA sequence to the right taxon or lineage, including when it is unlike anything in the reference?

attributes.question: Which method assigns a viral or microbial DNA sequence to the right taxon or lineage, including when it is unlike anything in the reference?
intended_users: Virologists assigning taxonomy or lineage to new viral sequences
Researchers classifying sequences from a metagenomic survey
attributes.decision: Choose a classifier, and decide whether a language model's embedding adds anything over an alignment search.
inputs: Sequences to classify, with their length
The reference database and its version
Whether the taxa of interest are in the reference
attributes.output: Classification accuracy or F1 at each taxonomic level, with an alignment baseline on the same sequences where one was run.
attributes.setting: Research virology and metagenomics. Clinical pathogen identification from patient samples has its own use cases.
exclusions: Clinical DNA and RNA pathogen detection from patient samples, which have their own use cases
attributes.clinical_scope: Research only. Nothing recorded here supports a clinical or diagnostic decision.
evidence_gaps: The linked evidence rests on two studies: Bůžková et al. 2026's RVDB viral classification, which also compares the best embedding with BLAST, and GenBench's species and SARS-CoV-2 variant tasks. Neither holds out whole genera, so 'unlike anything in the reference' is not tested.
ViroBench, which does hold out genera and deposit dates, is in the store, but its source carries an open evidence concern, so it is not linked. CAMI's protocol records are not reviewed.
Automated source review only. No human scientific review.

name: Relevance of gfm2-20261011-buzkova2026-protocol-acc-33 to use-case-viral-microbial-sequence-classification
description: Assigning viral sequences to one of 33 RVDB classes by nearest-neighbour retrieval over each model's embeddings: taxonomic assignment, the use case's endpoint.

attributes.endpoint: Assign the organism label of the single nearest indexed training sequence to each test sequence, comparing pooling strategies across nine models.
attributes.rationale: Assigning viral sequences to one of 33 RVDB classes by nearest-neighbour retrieval over each model's embeddings: taxonomic assignment, the use case's endpoint.
constraints: Compare rows only within this protocol: RVDB 33-class viral classification by nearest-neighbour retrieval over frozen embeddings (Bůžková et al. 2026 Table 3).
limitations: Nearest-neighbour probe over labelled reference embeddings, not zero-shot classification: the index holds the training labels (Section 2.7).
Point estimates from one fixed split with a fixed random seed; 95% Wilson intervals are quoted in the text, not in the tables.
RVDB organism labels are not a controlled taxonomy; the 33-class refinement removed seven ambiguous labels found through the models' own confusions (Sections 3.2 and 4).
